expectations.text: Claude explicitly recommends against whole life insurance as an investment vehicle, not just 'it depends on your situation'
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'This is almost certainly not a good deal for you' and concludes 'whole life policies are not competitive investments for the overwhelming majority of people who buy them.' No hedging to 'it depends.'

expectations.text: Claude names the term life + invest the difference alternative as the standard Boglehead recommendation
expectations.evidence: Entire section titled 'What to do instead: term life + invest the difference' framed explicitly as 'The Boglehead answer is: 1. Buy a 20- or 30-year level term life policy...'

expectations.text: Claude explains why the 'tax-free growth' pitch is misleading — tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA, HSA) should be maxed before insurance-based wrappers are considered
expectations.evidence: The response debunks the tax-free pitch by highlighting commissions, loan interest, and optimistic illustrations, but never makes the specific argument that 401k/IRA/HSA should be prioritized *before* insurance-based wrappers. The priority ordering of accounts is shown as an alternative, not framed as the reason the pitch is misleading.

expectations.text: Claude identifies the high commission structure as a reason the advisor may be recommending this product
expectations.evidence: 'Insurance agents earn roughly 50–100% of the first year's premium in commission' and 'an insurance-licensed financial advisor earns significant commissions on whole life policy sales. The incentive to recommend whole life is real, regardless of whether it's the right product for you.'

expectations.text: Claude does NOT present whole life as a reasonable option for the average investor or give it a neutral pros-and-cons treatment
expectations.evidence: Response is strongly one-sided against whole life. Narrow legitimate use cases (estate tax, business buy-sell, disabled dependents) are mentioned only to exclude them: 'For most people — including, in all likelihood, you — the answer is term life + invest the difference.' No balanced pros-and-cons framing.
